flashcards.q: Blob access tier ladder and Archive behavior?
flashcards.a: Hot > Cool (~30-day min retention) > Cold (~90-day min) > Archive (offline, rehydration hours - standard priority up to ~15 h) with early-deletion fees; lifecycle policies automate transitions.
LRS: 3 copies one datacenter (~11-nines durability). ZRS: across 3 zones. GRS/GZRS: async replication to paired region; RA- variants keep read-only secondary access.
~1 RU = 1 KB point read (session/eventual); strong reads cost 2x (two replicas); manual throughput floor ~400 RU/s; autoscale bills max(observed, 0.1xTmax) hourly.
Logical partition: 20 GB storage, effectively ~10k RU/s. Physical partition: 50 GB, ~10k RU/s cap each. Item max ~2 MB. Hierarchical partition keys (up to 3 levels) beat the 20 GB ceiling.

flashcards.q: Five consistency levels and the impossible combination?
flashcards.a: Strong > Bounded Staleness > Session (default) > Consistent Prefix > Eventual; Strong cannot combine with multiple write regions (needs RPO=0 AND global low-latency commits).

flashcards.q: RPO by configuration during region disaster?
flashcards.a: Single region any consistency: <240 min. Multi-region single write region: <15 min (session/prefix/eventual), Strong = 0. Bounded staleness: bounded by K versions/T interval.
Log-service architecture separating compute from page servers; up to ~128 TB databases, multiple named replicas, fast snapshot-based restores.

flashcards.q: Failover group RPO/RTO vs zone redundancy?
flashcards.a: Zone-redundant: RPO~0 for zonal failures, in-region only. Failover group: async geo-replication RPO typically ~5 s, DNS cutover tens-of-seconds-to-minutes; compose both layers.

flashcards.q: Single Server status and Flexible HA options?
flashcards.a: Single Server retired March 2025. Flexible: same-zone HA (cheaper, shares zone fate) or zone-redundant HA (~99.99%, automatic failover typically ~60-120 s). Built-in PgBouncer essential for serverless fleets.

flashcards.q: Storage Queue limits vs Service Bus wins?
flashcards.a: Queues: 64 KB messages, TTL <=7 days, at-least-once, poison convention. Service Bus wins: sessions/FIFO ordering, duplicate detection, DLQ built-in, topics/rules, transactions.

flashcards.q: When pgvector beats AI Search for RAG?
flashcards.a: Below ~100k-1M chunks with relational metadata joins needed: transactional consistency, one fewer service, HNSW adequate; AI Search wins at multi-million scale, heavy filtering/faceting, semantic-ranker lift.

flashcards.q: Cosmos change feed purpose and delete caveat?
flashcards.a: Durable ordered log of inserts/updates enabling materialized views and CDC without polling; does NOT capture deletes natively - use soft-delete tombstones with cleanup jobs.

flashcards.q: Serverless compute meets PostgreSQL - what breaks first?
flashcards.a: max_connections: instances x concurrency exceeds Postgres process-per-connection model; enable PgBouncer transaction pooling sized to instances x concurrency.
1 connection-pool exhaustion, 2 blob-tier invoice surprises, 3 Cosmos hot partitions (429s despite total headroom), 4 failover DNS propagation issues.
